name: Haze from MODIS satellites
summary: Satellite measurements of haze (aerosol optical depth) in 1 km pixels from the MODIS instruments, once a day. A candidate: needs a free NASA Earthdata login and is not connected yet.

el.name: Θολούρα από τους δορυφόρους MODIS
el.summary: Δορυφορικές μετρήσεις θολούρας (οπτικό βάθος αερολυμάτων) σε εικονοστοιχεία 1 km από τα όργανα MODIS, μία φορά την ημέρα. Υποψήφια πηγή: χρειάζεται δωρεάν σύνδεση NASA Earthdata και δεν έχει συνδεθεί ακόμη.

publisher.name: NASA (MODIS MCD19A2, distributed by LP DAAC)

licence.attribution: MODIS MCD19A2 (MAIAC) aerosol data from NASA LP DAAC. NASA is acknowledged as the source.

restrictions: Needs a free NASA Earthdata login
AppEEARS works in steps: submit a task, wait, download a table

update.note: Daily composite. How soon after the pass it is available was not checked.

variables.note: Band Optical_Depth_055 (name from the MAIAC guide, not yet checked in AppEEARS).

quality.uncertainty: Haze in the whole air column in 1 km pixels, only where there is no cloud, from one or two passes a day. The size of the error was not checked.
known_issues: Cloud leaves gaps, sometimes for days.
A satellite sees haze but cannot tell dust from smoke or sea salt by itself.
The CAMS model takes MODIS haze data in, so model and MODIS are not independent.

upstream.name: MODIS instruments on the Terra and Aqua satellites

use_for: Checking the haze of the CAMS model against what a satellite sees
Showing a Saharan dust day from space

notes: Not connected. Checked on 2026-11-12: the ORNL DAAC MODIS web service lists land products and its documentation names no aerosol product, so it is not a route to haze. NASA AppEEARS may offer MCD19A2 for a point (ask GET /product); it needs an Earthdata login (user name and password) and several steps per request.
